newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer, September takes over as benchmark.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer, September takes over as benchmark.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer on Wednesday after two days of losses.
The market now considers the September contract to be the new benchmark because its turnover exceeded that of the June this morning, traders said.

Buying related to the benchmark shift was a key factor behind Wednesday's rise. But some traders attributed the firmness to other factors, including an accommodative Bank of Japan (BOJ) operation, proposed cuts in government spending, lacklustre stocks and a wire service report which said Japanese manufacturers' sentiment worsened in May compared with April.
The September ended up 0.39 at 122.74, but off the session high of 122.87. Turnover was 47,089 contracts.
The previous benchmark, the June contract, was up 0.45 at 124.20 in a turnover of 30,338 contracts.
"I didn't see any particular factors determining the market today except for buying of the relatively cheap September contract," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.
He said, however, the rise may have been partly due to reaction to fiscal reform proposals announced late on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

On Tuesday, Hashimoto set numerical targets for proposed cuts in a wide range of government spending areas, including previously untouchable areas such as public works, defence and agricultural assistance.
This raised concerns among some in the market about a possible negative impact on Japan's economic recovery and a possible decline in JGB issues, which helped spurred buying of JGBs, traders said.
"I didn't take the reform so seriously. But some followed sentiment amid a lack of fresh news until the BOJ's 'tankan' survey," said a dealer at a "Big Four" brokerage house.
The BOJ's quarterly tankan corporate sentiment survey is set to be released on June 25.

Some traders said the market got support from a foreign wire service survey, conducted in the same way as the BOJ's tankan, showing that Japanese manufacturers' sentiment, as reflected in the diffusion index, worsened to 17 in May compared with April's 23.
But others said they were unaware of the report.
In the cash market, dealers' short-covering emerged at the long-end of the yield curve, traders said.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB stood at 2.510 percent at 0728 GMT, sharply down from Tuesday's 2.560 percent.

This is the level last seen before JGB yields jumped on May 21, when BOJ deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted as saying that the central bank is considering the right time to raise the discount rate.

"Given weak industrial output data last week, fears of higher interest rates (which heightened after BOJ deputy governor Fukui's remark) have subsided. But the market was still hesitant to rise, with the topside heavy at a price of par for the last auctioned 2.7 percent 10-year JGB," said the "Big Four" brokerage dealer. -- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
